findings.reason: the rule and its control must be scoped to a live, non-exhausted name (or to the dead-end stages the ruling covers), otherwise the worker either breaks a passing test or writes a control that cannot fire.
findings.text: §11 makes the rule "returns a held source to the pool only when the name holding it is exhausted" and orders "a test [that] fails when the pass is allowed to take the source of a name that is not exhausted", but the pass it names is `reconcile_source_status_liveness`, whose terminal set is `superseded`, `exhausted` and `contested` (`imas_codex/standard_names/graph_store/graph_foundation.py:108-114`), which deliberately resets a `composed` source whose only target is a `superseded` name back to `extracted` (`graph_audits.py:841-922`; that behaviour is asserted today by `tests/standard_names/test_source_revival.py:251` (plants `name_stage = 'superseded'`) and `:423` (`assert state["status"] == "extracted"`), so the stated negative control fires on correct behaviour and a literal implementation would strand every superseded name's source out of the generation pool

findings.reason: the section is dispatched on that one log line, and committing the excerpt or quoting its exact message is what pins the pass the retirement rule is to be applied to.
findings.text: §11 opens on the pass whose "log reads 24 returned to 'extracted'" and identifies it as "the one that reconciles each source's status with whether a live name still holds it", but that pass logs `"%d returned to extracted"` with no quotes, and the only quoted occurrences are `"%d source(s) returned to 'extracted' so compose rewrites the missing prose"` (`graph_audits.py:2345`, the descriptionless pass §11 itself calls a different path that keeps its behaviour) and `"%d of %d source(s) returned to 'extracted' …"` (`loop.py:1872,1891`); no file under `docs/evidence/fragments/sn-pipeline-hygiene/` carries the line, so a worker cannot tell which of four maintenance passes emitted the count and the attribution rests entirely on paraphrase
